text:
casey_support: Hey team, escalating a customer issue — they see intermittent 401 then 403 for the same endpoint /v1/generate. Customer says it started after a key rotation yesterday. Req IDs in one session: req=01a2b3c4, req=01a2b3c5.

customer_ops: Confirmed — they rotated both org-scoped and project-scoped keys. Some clients might be still sending the old X-Org header.

devik: Can you paste the raw curl they used and any request headers? Common culprit is org/project header swap or a service token used against a project-scoped resource.

customer_ops: Here's what we captured from their curl (sanitized):

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_*****" \
  -H "X-Project: proj-9a7" \
  -H "X-Org: org-3b2" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

customer_ops: When it fails they get 401 with body: `{"error":{"code":"unauthorized","message":"invalid credentials"}}` and request id header `x-rw-req: 01a2b3c4`. When it returns 403 it's `x-rw-req: 01a2b3c5` with body `quota exceeded` even though customer is under quota.

inga_jenkins: Interesting — two different codes for same session. Could be token scope mismatch vs signature verification error. Devs: can we check auth service logs for those req ids and correlate to key id used?

devik: On it. Pulling logs for 01a2b3c4 and 01a2b3c5 now.

deploy-bot: log-pull started for reqs [01a2b3c4,01a2b3c5] by devik at 2026-03-17T10:12:30Z

devik: Quick notes from auth logs: 
- 01a2b3c4 -> signature verification failed against public key id sk-rot-2026-03-16 (expected sk-prod-2025), returned 401.
- 01a2b3c5 -> token validated but policy check failed: token scope = project:proj-9a7, attempted access to org-scoped route -> returned 403 (quota check block).

casey_support: So they have a mix: some requests still signed with rotated key, others using new key but wrong scope header. Customer rotated keys but part of their fleet didn't pick up new key and some microservices are sending project header to org routes.

ashley_pm: Action items: 1) ask customer to confirm all instances updated with new key (sk-rot-2026-03-16 replacement). 2) Ask them to run a targeted curl showing both headers + Authorization and capture x-rw-req for failures. 3) We should provide a small script to detect stale key use.

casey_support: I'll send repro steps. Proposed curl to run repeatedly to reproduce both behaviors:

```
for i in {1..20}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{header_x_rw_req}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_KEY" \
    -H "X-Org: org-3b2" \
    -H "X-Project: proj-9a7" \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  sleep 0.5
done
```

casey_support: Also asked them to attach a debug bundle (curl -D - trace) and we gave them a signed upload URL.

inga_jenkins: We'll also add a temporary auth-service check to surface mixed-key usage in the console for their org. Might help them find stale containers.

devik: Logged a follow-up internal ticket RW-INT-8452 to add an alert when we see both signature failures and scope-deny responses within same source IP over a short window.

customer_ops: Customer ran the loop and captured both behaviors. Uploaded debug bundle to the link we provided. Uploaded file id: db-20260317-77f.

casey_support: Thanks — I'll attach bundle to the support case and mark triage complete. Final reply to customer: steps to rotate all keys, validate headers, and run our scan. Will provide the script and timeline. :thumbsup:

devik: If we want a quick mitigation: allow fallback rule for 5m where rotated key ID accepted for old signature algorithm while customers finish rollout — but that needs approvals.

inga_jenkins: Noted. Ops/SEC signoff required. For now we can provide clear repro steps and the scan script.

casey_support: Closing thread once customer confirms roll. Refs: reqs [01a2b3c4,01a2b3c5], debug bundle db-20260317-77f, internal RW-INT-8452.
